A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TaDSE research despite the changed title and organization. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable content matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original intent-classification experiments on five dialogue datasets, augmentation and loss ablations, compression experiments, and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results including expanded ablations, compression tests, and black-box embedding comparisons in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The augmentation procedure, three loss components, optional MLP, and compression variants are retained. However, Eqs. 1–2 remove dropout-view superscripts from denominator embeddings without explaining whether this changes the implemented objective or merely its notation. A procedural change cannot be established reliably.

E1.justification: Both versions use SNIPS, ATIS, MASSIVE, HWU64, and CLINC150 for English dialogue intent classification. Additional analyses and black-box comparisons use these retained datasets. General embedding benchmarks are discussed as excluded, while medical, legal, and cross-domain evaluations remain future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds a distinct comparator family: text-embedding-3-small, text-embedding-3-large, and gemini-embedding-001 are evaluated against TaDSE on SNIPS and ATIS in Table 12. The original BERT, SimCSE, TOD-BERT, and DSE comparison remains; changing the augmented variants' suffix from 'aug' to 'ours' is only renaming.

E3.justification: v2 adds top-4 slot-value augmentation settings for SNIPS, MASSIVE, and CLINC150, and specifies 768-dimensional outputs for the new black-box comparisons. The retained learning rate, epoch budgets, batch size, kNN evaluation, and validation-based compression selection are unchanged. Expanded training descriptions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 extends loss ablations to CLINC150 and compression tests to MASSIVE and CLINC150, exposing mixed or negative outcomes absent from v1's SNIPS/ATIS compression comparison. It also adds top-4 sensitivity points, expands uniformity/alignment analysis to four datasets, and adds an uncompressed TaDSE ATIS visualization. The original kNN and training-epoch analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard errors, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; the asterisks in v2 Figure 6 identify best-performing models rather than statistical significance.

E6.justification: All 54 numerical entries in the main comparison are unchanged between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2. Substantial supplementary results are added: for Lu + Lt + Lpair, v2 Table 5 reports compressed/uncompressed accuracy of 78.24/79.39 on MASSIVE and 72.25/72.98 on CLINC150. Table 12 shows TaDSE leading the black-box models on ATIS and the two-dataset average, but trailing on SNIPS. Existing SNIPS/ATIS uniformity-alignment coordinates also change without explanation.

T1.justification: Eqs. 1–2 change mathematically as written: denominator arguments t_j^+ and u_j^+ become t_j and u_j, while numerator positives retain their dropout-view superscripts. This limited formulation revision is unexplained. The pairwise loss and uniformity/alignment definitions remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions and dialogue-performance claims remain. v2 adds an explicit conclusion claim of being first to employ dialogue-template semantics for dialogue embeddings, removes the introduction's quantified 7–40-fold augmentation claim, and gives visualization-based support greater prominence in the contribution list.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses inconclusive compression results on MASSIVE/CLINC150, qualifies the alignment-based performance explanation, and warns that more compression need not improve accuracy. New Appendix B explains the exclusion of general embedding benchmarks. Expanded limitations address restricted slot-value diversity, discrete compression search, untested cross-domain transfer, and language-specific tokenization.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies pooled-source training for the main table and checkpoint-based, Lu-only training for augmented baselines. v2 also clarifies that shared SLOT replacement follows augmentation and specifies black-box embedding dimensions. Core hardware and hyperparameters are retained. The code-release promise changes from 'soon' to 'upon acceptance'; neither PDF supplies released code.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through a slot-filling/intent-classification related-work discussion, comparisons with rule-based augmentation and backtranslation, and a dialogue-versus-general-embedding evaluation argument. Added references include Louvan and Magnini, Dialog2Flow, MTEB, BEIR, and recent general embedding studies. Several broad vision/background references disappear with the background rewrite.

P1.justification: v2 removes the standalone sentence-embedding background section and incorporates condensed contrastive-learning background into the introduction. It extensively rewrites the introduction, contributions, method explanations, and limitations, reorganizes the appendices, and standardizes terminology from entities/alignment layers toward slots/MLP variants. The title and author affiliations also change.

P2.justification: v1 Table 2 becomes the illustrated augmentation diagram in v2 Figure 3, and the system diagram is redrawn. Separate uniformity/alignment plots are replaced by a combined four-dataset figure with new axes, symbols, arrows, and annotations. Several result tables gain columns, a black-box comparison table is added, and the ATIS appendix gains an uncompressed TaDSE plot.

improvement.justification: v2 improves assessment of the work by reporting compression failures beyond SNIPS/ATIS, adding black-box comparisons, and clarifying baseline training and applicability limits. These are useful gains over unchanged main performance results. Their overall benefit is limited by unexplained changes to the loss denominators and uniformity/alignment coordinates, which leave important formulation and reproducibility questions unresolved.
